samples.summary: `sheets export --file-format csv` inherits the new CSV formula neutralization and corrupts exported data
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:46 calls the shared `formatCsv(res.data)` directly (not through `output()`), so the new `neutralizeFormula` in packages/cli/src/output/csv.ts now prefixes every exported formula/value starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR with `'`. That path is a file/stdout export of sheet content, not a human-facing render: the documented pipeline `wafflebase sheets export "$DOC_ID" out.csv` (packages/cli/skills/recipe-csv-pipeline.md:44, docs/design/cli.md:1064) exports cells that contain `=SUM(B2:B100)` and re-imports them via `sheets import` (parseCsv → buildCellMap), which will now write the literal text `'=SUM(B2:B100)`. The design doc scopes the neutralization to the `--format csv` render path only (docs/design/cli.md:854-858) and says nothing about `--file-format csv` export, so this consumer was not considered. Fix belongs on the new code: keep neutralization in the `output()`/`format()` path (or make it opt-in) rather than inside `formatCsv` itself.

samples.summary: CLI now requires the backend to echo the nonce; against any backend without this change login can never succeed
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:227 rejects every callback whose `state` does not match the nonce, and deliberately never settles the promise, so the only outcome against a backend that does not echo `state` is the 30s timeout at login.ts:280-288. The CLI is published separately and points at a user-supplied `--server` (packages/cli/src/config/config.ts DEFAULT_SERVER / `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER`), so a newer CLI talking to an older/self-hosted backend (which ignores `nonce` in the guard and emits `?code=` with no `state`) breaks `wafflebase login` outright. No version negotiation or compatibility fallback exists anywhere in the flow.

samples.summary: rest-api.md still documents the loopback redirect contract without the echoed `state=<nonce>`
samples.evidence: docs/design/rest-api.md:334-342 describes `GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=<port>` and a callback that redirects to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=<auth-code>` — no `nonce` query param and no `state` on the redirect. docs/design/cli.md:175-207 was updated for the new contract; the backend-surface doc was not, so the two design docs now disagree about the same endpoint.

Run `wafflebase login`.\")" as the justification for resolving the workspace by re-reading config/session files instead of asking the CLI. packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts now emits `{ loggedIn, ... }` through `output()`, so the stated rationale is stale and the duplicated resolution logic is now avoidable (the same text exists in .trusted/scripts/agent/hunt-workspace.mjs:17).

samples.summary: `ctx switch` still prints prose on a missing session while the doc row this change relies on covers all session-required commands
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:94 does `console.error('Not logged in. Run `wafflebase login`.')` + `process.exit(1)`, and ctx.ts:100 does the same for a missing workspace, so neither emits the `{ error: { code: 'NOT_LOGGED_IN' | ... } }` envelope. docs/design/cli.md:1105 documents the NOT_LOGGED_IN envelope for "`ctx list` (and other session-required commands) without a session". `ctx switch` also never calls `parseOutputFormat`, so `--format bogus` is still silently accepted there.

samples.summary: `cells batch --dry-run` now runs outside any try/catch, unlike every other dry-run call site
samples.evidence: After the restructure the dry-run branch sits at packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:147-155 with no enclosing try, so a throw from `getConfig(opts)` (config/session resolution, `migrateConfigIfNeeded` file copy) or `printDryRun` escapes as an unhandled action-promise rejection instead of reaching `outputError` — the exact failure mode the new comment at cells.ts:117-121 says must not happen. Every other dry-run site (docs.ts:102, notes.ts:62, slides.ts:67, tabs.ts, files.ts) still wraps this in try/catch. `--format` is likewise not validated on the dry-run path here, unlike the request path.

samples.summary: Commands that do not render through `output()` still silently accept a bogus global `--format`, so the change's rule is only half applied
samples.evidence: The branch's thesis is that a bad `--format` fails loudly, but `sheets export` (packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:13, which validates only its own `--file-format`), `files upload`/`files download`, `sheets import`'s file format, and `docs/slides/notes import` never call `parseOutputFormat`, so `--format bogus` is accepted and ignored on those commands while it is exit-1 INVALID_FORMAT on their siblings. This is an inconsistency in the surviving call sites, not in the diff itself.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `neutralizeFormula` is applied inside `formatCsv` itself (packages/cli/src/output/csv.ts:23-47), so it affects every consumer, not just the render path. `packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:46` imports and calls `formatCsv(res.data)` directly (import at sheets-export.ts:6), bypassing `output()`/`parseOutputFormat`, and writes the result to a file or stdout (sheets-export.ts:48-51). The payload is `getCells` (sheets-export.ts:39; http-client.ts:340), documented to carry a `formula` field such as `"=A1+1"` (docs/design/cli.md:902-904, docs/design/rest-api.md:203), which will now be emitted as `'=A1+1`. The re-import path applies no un-quoting (sheets-import.ts:73,81 -> parseCsv/buildCellMap), so the documented export/import round trip (docs/design/cli.md:1064, packages/cli/skills/recipe-csv-pipeline.md:44, packages/cli/skills/sheets-import-export.md:86) writes literal quoted text back into cells. The design doc scopes the neutralization to the `--format csv` render path only (docs/design/cli.md:854-858) and never mentions `--file-format csv` export. No guard or opt-out exists on the export path, and there is no test covering `sheets export`. This is a behaviour change to an exported symbol with an unconsidered consumer — in-lane for blast radius, and data-corrupting, so blocking.

verdict.reason: The quoted CLI code is real (login.ts:227 rejects non-matching `state` without settling; only the 30s timeout at login.ts:280-288 remains), but it is not a blast-radius defect. Grepping every reference to the nonce/state contract shows the sole counterpart consumer in this repository is fully updated: github-auth.guard.ts:39 parses `?nonce=`, cli-auth.store.ts:13/30/38/60 round-trips it, and auth.controller.ts:131-135 echoes it as `&state=` on the loopback redirect. No in-repo caller, entry point, or sibling package is left on the old form, and the reverse skew (old CLI, new backend) is explicitly preserved by the `state.nonce ? … : ''` conditional at auth.controller.ts:131-133 (asserted in auth.controller.spec.ts:234). The only failing combination is a newer published CLI against an out-of-repo, previously deployed backend — a release/rollout coupling, not an unupdated call site; the finding names no file:line that needs to change other than the new code itself, and it is stateable entirely from login.ts without leaving the diff, which the lens defines as another lens's lane (correctness already logs it at .agent-review/correctness/verdict.json:47). The coupling is also an explicit documented contract at docs/design/cli.md:206-208 (cited as evidence of intent only; repo text treated as data).
